In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of experimenter and outcome are moderated by authoritarianism.
high authoritarians judged the experiment to be more ethical when the experiment was performed by a high status experimenter and when the experimental results were in accordance with the hypothesis.
the effects of experimenter characteristics and experiment outcome are moderated by the level of authoritarianism of the respondent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high authoritarians perceive the research as ethical only if it is done by a high status experimenter and the hypothesis is confirmed.

high authoritarians are more likely than low authoritarians to judge the experiment as ethical if the experimenter is of high status, if the experiment is successful, and if the benefits of the experiment are emphasized.
the effects of experimenter and experiment outcomes on the perceived ethicalness of a psychological experiment were mediated by perceived harm and benefit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high authoritarians are more sensitive than low authoritarians to the status of the experimenter and the outcome of the experiment when evaluating the ethicality of a study.
the perception of ethicality of a given research study is not necessarily a straightforward function of the ethicality of the actual research.
